requirement:
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.

A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions` that needs implementation evidence. The review roots are empty, and the requirement has no Implements edges, only four Tests edges. I checked each clause against a behavior-preserving alternative implementation.

- **"MAY satisfy the coverage policy only through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence"**: This describes when an exception is valid. An implementation could use any evidence store or checker that accepts and rejects the same cases, so no library, type or interface is mandated.
- **"attached to the source file or function whose incomplete coverage it justifies"**, "MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions" and "MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage": These are scoping rules on outcomes. They set which items an exception covers, not how the code is built. Any data layout that keeps exceptions from covering other items satisfies them.
- **"Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under `requirements.references.citation_review`"**: The observable obligation is that a change invalidates the exception. `requirements.references.citation_review` is cited, not implemented, and it defines the staleness rules. Separate hash tracking that invalidates the same exceptions would behave identically, so reusing the citation-review mechanism is discretionary. The citation-review record and staleness rules belong to that requirement's own assessment.
- **"A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted exception evidence"**: This is observable acceptance behavior.
- **"Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between equivalent local and CI checkouts"**: This is an observable property of the produced identities. Any scheme that yields the same identity across checkouts conforms, so the text prescribes no particular type, field or algorithm.

Every clause specifies observable behavior, which the existing test edges cover. Nothing here calls for an `{impl}` marker.

behavioral: All four reviewed tests carry `{test}` markers for `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. I did not read implementation source. Together they cover each behavioral obligation in the requirement.

- **File exception does not excuse functions.** In `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution]`, the file has an accepted file-level cite and an unexplained function `a` with zero execution. The report fails, shows the file line as an accepted exception, and still lists `#fn[a]: zero execution`.
- **A function exception satisfies the policy.** In the same test, adding a function-level cite lets the report pass. The accepted-exceptions section lists both the file threshold and `#fn[a]: zero execution`. The not-measured function case is also listed as accepted, and an unmeasured file is accepted as an exception.
- **An exception covers only its own item.** `fn[function_explanations_never_transfer_to_other_functions_or_the_file]` tries an outer-function exception and an inner-function exception. In each case only the explained function is waived, and the other functions still show `zero execution; requires`. A function exception also does not rescue the file threshold, because the report still shows `code.rs: 0/1 (0.0%) — FAIL`. An unmeasured other file still fails.
- **Only current, accepted, assessed evidence counts.** In `fn[missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report]`, source comments alone with no review give "missing citation review" and a FAIL. Reviews with determination `false` or `{FIXME}` also leave the file failing. The first test checks the "determination is false" and "cannot accept a {fixme}" messages.
- **Invalidation on change.** In `fn[missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report]`, a changed file rationale gives a FAIL, and a changed function rationale gives "citations changed". Changing the function body gives "outline input changed". In each case the function is no longer excused. `fn[standard_inline_doc_and_fenced_commentary_reviews_track_their_explanations]` also checks that editing an inline doc comment or fenced commentary makes the exception not accepted and reports an error.
- **Portability.** The last part of `fn[standard_inline_doc_and_fenced_commentary_reviews_track_their_explanations]` copies the evidence file into a different temporary checkout. The exception is still accepted with no errors, so identities do not depend on checkout paths. The coverage records use varying run identifiers, and the reports and exception identities (`code.rs#fn[a]`) stay stable across them.

The citation-review mechanics for a changed cited declaration belong to `requirements.references.citation_review` and are cited context here. I found no unaddressed obligation and no assertion that contradicts the requirement.

text: :::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
other than a citation of `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. For citations
of project requirements and examples, the reviewer MUST assess whether the item
should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition changes, and
whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead.
For citations of built-ins, the reviewer MUST check the permitted reference
roles and forms and any citation-review criteria stated in the built-in's fixed
text, using the item's source and commentary. A permitted citation role alone
MUST NOT suffice when the fixed text states additional criteria. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
Fenced commentary elsewhere in the book is reviewed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary`.
Storage MAY use the versioned representation under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_format`, retaining the same review
information and validation rules.
